Checked against the authorities and the endocrine finding does not exist: ATSDR's profile reports no gross or microscopic alterations in pituitary, adrenal, thyroid or parathyroid tissues across the published studies, and states no further information was located on endocrine effects. The SVHC entry's environmental concern is persistence and mobility, not endocrine activity, and the substance is not on the EU endocrine disruptor lists. An ED screening test having been run is not a positive finding. Harmonized classification is Carc 1B H350, Eye Irrit 2 H319, STOT SE 3 H335, Flam Liq 2 H225: no dermal and no reproductive classification to trace to. canc A retained, it traces to H350.
reclassified: 1,4-dioxane was historically treated as a harmless manufacturing byproduct in ethoxylated surfactants. Now recognized as a probable human carcinogen (IARC 2B). NY State banned it in cleaning products above 1 ppm (2023). EU considering REACH restriction.

Diethylene Glycol.note: Graded from PubChem GHS (CID 8117, title 'Diethylene Glycol'): the dominant ECHA C&L block (38 notifications / 5754 reports) reports H302 100% (harmful if swallowed - acute oral toxicity is not one of the graded dimensions). Diethylene Glycol.s: Harmful if swallowed; glycol solvent/corrosion inhibitor.

Diethylene Glycol Monobutyl Ether.note: Corrected 2026-10-10 (Sifter verify vs PubChem CID 8177, title 'Diethylene Glycol Monobutyl Ether' - matches; CAS 112-34-5): H302 in the prior g is not in the ECHA C&L consensus (headline block is H319 >99.9% only; H227/H336/H371/H372 appear in minority notifier blocks) - removed per the Benzotriazole 2026-09-24 precedent. derm C traces to H319 >99.9% (eye irritant). reclassified: DEGBE is a glycol ether — the same family as 2-butoxyethanol (EGBE). Lower acute toxicity than EGBE, but the class concern stands.
Diethylene Glycol Monobutyl Ether.s: DEGBE — glycol ether solvent used in heavy-duty oven and floor cleaners. Serious eye irritant (H319). Glycol-ether class carries reproductive/developmental concern in EU/Prop 65 classifications.

Diethylester Dimethyl Ammonium Chloride.note: UVCB (CAS 919-30-2). PubChem returns no CID for the name (PUG REST 404). Recorded extrapolated by quat class rather than invented — the class hazards are skin/eye irritation and aquatic toxicity (see the existing 'Quaternary Ammonium' entry).

Ethanol.note: Graded from PubChem GHS (CID 702). repro.mechanism: Ethanol is a known human teratogen. The reproductive concern is a developmental one that GHS does not encode: the record's own g carries H225 only, with no harmonised reproductive classification.

repro.quote_note: Route caveat, and it matters: the EPA record this passage comes from is an inhalation study in rats, and the FASD effects it cites are from ingestion at high doses. The passage establishes that ethanol is a known human teratogen; it does not establish a risk from a cleaning-product exposure. Read it as the basis for a documented mechanism, not as a finding about household use.

Ethanolamine.s: Corrosive amine. Occupational asthma documented in cleaners (meta-analyses).

DEP is used as a solvent for fragrance and was the most frequently detected phthalate in this study's consumer products, at its highest concentrations in fragranced items. The record's own g carries H317 only; GHS does not encode endocrine activity.
endo.quote: DEP, a common solvent for fragrance (Hubinger and Havery 2006), was detected most frequently; the highest DEP concentrations were in fragrance/perfume (14,000 µg/g) and car air freshener (8,000 µg/g).
endo.quote_note: The study also found none of the tested products listed 'phthalate' on the label, so the route is real but unlabelled. The passage establishes the fragrance-to-phthalate route and the phthalate class; it does not grade DEP itself.

organ.mechanism: Ingested oxalic acid is a nephrotoxin: it precipitates as calcium oxalate in the renal tubules, and the resulting tubular injury is the organ-level harm. The record's own g carries H302,H312 only, with no H373 and no organ code, so the organ grade cannot trace to g.
organ.quote: Precipitation of calcium oxalate in the renal system (proximal tubules of the kidney) may lead to local necrosis of the tubular epithelium, producing kidney dysfunction and electrolyte imbalance
organ.quote_note: From a peer-reviewed case report of acute renal failure after oxalic acid ingestion (Dassanayake & Gnanathasan 2012, J Occup Med Toxicol 7:17, DOI 10.1186/1745-6673-7-17). The route in the source is ingestion; the case report notes oxalic acid is a component of household laundry detergents in the region studied. It establishes the renal mechanism, not a dose-response for cleaning use.

alpha-Isomethyl Ionone.s: Fragrance ketone (ionone family). Skin sensitizer; toxic to aquatic life with long lasting effects.
alpha-Isomethyl Ionone.note: Graded from PubChem GHS (CID 5372174, CAS 127-51-5, title '3-Methyl-4-(2,6,6-trimethyl-2-cyclohexen-1-yl)-3-buten-2-one'): ECHA C&L notifier consensus H317 88.6%, H315 78.1%, H319 70.7% -> derm D + allerg; H411 87.7% -> env D. H412 (10.2%) is below the 40% bar. An EU fragrance allergen (Reg. 1223/2009 Annex III) with no equivalent US cleaning-product labelling requirement. Disclosed as a fragrance allergen by Clean Control Corporation in the CA SB-258 declaration for OdoBan Ready-to-Use (Original Eucalyptus Scent).

Ethoxydiglycol.s: Glycol ether (fragrance component). Not classified at the house threshold; a low-consensus organ-toxicity notification exists.
Ethoxydiglycol.note: Graded from PubChem GHS (CID 8146, CAS 111-90-0, title 'Diethylene Glycol Monoethyl Ether'): the ECHA C&L aggregate reports no hazard criteria met by 4397 of 4862 reports (90.4%). 11 notifications covering 465 of 4862 reports (9.6%) carry H227, H320 and H372 - all far below the 40% house bar, so no dimension grade is justified. H372 (organ damage on prolonged or repeated exposure) is noted here rather than graded, because a 9.6% notification ratio is not a consensus. Disclosed as a fragrance component by Reckitt SmartLabel for Vanish Oxi Action In-Wash Fabric Stain Remover; the disclosure flags it on California's toxic air contaminant list.
